key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost with far fewer simulations than tested black-box baselines.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports sizing and configuring eight energy technologies, including photovoltaics and storage, rather than optimizing solar-cell devices.
method: Propose configuration changes using simulation history and structured agent memory.
Evaluate 25-year net present cost through year-long energy simulations.
Keep successful changes, revert unsuccessful ones via git, and log each decision.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load building case, agent trials used 50 simulations per run versus 300 for baselines; Opus reached the best design in all ten runs and came within 1% after a median of 18 simulations.
watch_item: Results from one building case do not establish generalization across climates, tariffs, or load profiles, and LLM operating costs require consideration.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
